name: How does drywall finishing in a basement differ from above-ground rooms?

mainEntity.name: How does drywall finishing in a basement differ from above-ground rooms?

acceptedAnswer.text: Moisture management is the most critical difference between basement drywall and upper-floor installations. Basement walls sit against below-grade foundation concrete, which can transmit moisture and temperature shifts. Standard drywall on upper levels handles stable humidity, but basements often require moisture-resistant drywall, often called green board or purple board, especially near perimeter foundations, bathrooms, and utility areas. Before finishing basement drywall, framing must be isolated from direct concrete contact with proper vapor barriers or rigid insulation. Skipping proper moisture preparation can trap dampness behind finished walls, leading to soft drywall, mold growth, or peeling paint later on.
acceptedAnswer.description: Basement drywall requires extra protection against below-grade moisture, including moisture-resistant boards and proper insulation spacing before taping and mudding.
